name: ctp-core-iorn-001-measurement
scope: The measurement module ctp_measure.py, the dataset-access module unitobrain.py, the six drivers that produce every number in paper/results/, and their tests. Pure computation over NumPy arrays and scalars, plus DICOM reading in unitobrain.py. No network access, no GUI, no patient data and no clinical claim. The UniToBrain data these run on are public, de-identified and openly licensed; none of it is included here, and no local path is included either: unitobrain.py takes the dataset's location from the UNITOBRAIN_ROOT environment variable and has no default, which a test enforces for every file in the snapshot. Out of scope and deliberately not sent: the ctp_core package itself (its own suite is pytest-style, which this cross-check v1 cannot run), figure rendering, and the manuscript.
requirements:
These files produce the numbers a manuscript will report, so each must hold exactly the property it is relied on for.

ctp_measure.py. (1) sampled_peak_time returns the argmax of a sampled curve and therefore only ever a value present in the given time axis; mismatched or empty inputs raise ValueError. (2) fitted_peak_time implements a validity rule: a fitted peak time is admitted only when the fit succeeded, the value is finite, and it lies within the closed acquisition window; otherwise it returns no value together with the reason. This rule exists because the curve fitter it guards reports success for peak times far outside the acquisition -- -32 s and +919 s were observed on a 0-44 s acquisition -- and admitting those moved a hemispheric mean from +0.24 s to +17.9 s. (3) quantisation_floor returns dt/sqrt(12), the standard deviation of a value rounded to a grid of spacing dt, and rejects a non-positive dt. (4) curve_area integrates only the positive part of an enhancement curve. (5) cbv_from_areas returns tissue area over arterial area scaled for density, so that an arterial area understated by a factor k inflates CBV by exactly k; a non-positive arterial area raises. The measured median k over 15 public cases was 6.97. (6) hemispheres splits a 2-D mask at the column centroid of the mask, not at the image centre, and the two parts must be disjoint and together cover the mask; an empty mask raises.

unitobrain.py. (7) load() must refuse a ragged volume rather than silently stacking one, and must refuse a case whose time vector, arterial input and number of acquisitions disagree. (8) tissue_mask admits a voxel only when its baseline attenuation is plausible and a bolus actually arrived; busiest_slice returns the slice with the most such voxels. (9) root() must be redirectable by UNITOBRAIN_ROOT, because the dataset is not redistributed with the repository.

The drivers. (10) run_screen.py chooses the figure case by a rule frozen before it was run -- largest absolute left-right median TTP difference in the dataset's own reference maps -- and aborts rather than ranking a partially extracted set. The median, not the mean, is deliberate; so is taking the midline from the mask. (11) run_clinical.py draws a fixed number of voxels per hemisphere with a fixed seed, and must draw them once per case so that the two input series and the two methods are compared on the same voxels; its docstring claims a standard error of about 0.05 s against an effect of about 5 s. (12) run_synthetic.py jitters bolus arrival across one sampling interval, because an arrival always landing on a sampling instant would make the fit-free path unbiased by construction and the whole comparison vacuous. (13) run_aif.py and run_reference.py must save enough to recompute what they report. (14) run_propagation.py must straddle the point at which the implementation's clips make an arterial error invisible in the maps.

Please look for ways any of these could be wrong or could degrade silently, including numerical edge cases, floating-point behaviour, and any place where a driver's result would change without a test going red. Say plainly where a test asserts less than the requirement it claims to cover. Note that prove_driver_gates.py exists to demonstrate the tests by injection and reports 14 of 14 defects caught by the test that claims to catch each one; if any of those injections could pass for the wrong reason, say so.
